problem: Key says "none" for a chained-subagent answer, while S003's key for the same subagent mechanism concedes a version-gated fact in its own parenthetical ("subagents run in the background by default as of v2.1.198"). Two keys therefore disagree about whether subagents carry a version caveat at all. Sheets that cite the same real v2.1.198 change (the /agents panel becoming a path printout) read as correct under S003's phrasing and as unrequested extra under S008's. Graded to the key: any sheet asserting no flag, no plan gate and no experimental status was credited 1 under S008.

Internally inconsistent with its own failure_mode key. failure_mode asserts that "background subagents (the default) also run with a reduced built-in tool set", a behaviour the same key dates to v2.1.198, yet version_caveat is keyed as "none". A sheet cannot be right on both fields at once without contradicting itself, so the pair is unscoreable as written. Graded to the key anyway.

The experimental env flag requirement (CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1) is keyed into BOTH lifecycle and version_caveat. A sheet that states the flag once, in version_caveat where it most naturally belongs, is scored down on lifecycle for a fact it did in fact report. The same duplication exists in S004 and S009. Recommend the flag live in one field only. Graded to the key: lifecycle credit was given where the spawn-and-confirm trigger was described, without requiring the flag to be repeated.

Key rejects "a dynamic workflow with a review stage and a verify stage", but S001's key credits exactly a fan-out-plus-verifier-stage workflow as the correct primary. The two keys separate the same shape only by item count (5 to 10 versus 400) with no keyed threshold anywhere in the scenario text, and S010's scenario wording ("none of the per-finding verification chatter should ever reach my conversation") argues for the workflow runtime as strongly as for nesting. Three of four sheets chose workflow here; all were scored 0 on primary per the key.

Key names 'Appending the conventions to the project CLAUDE.md', but the scenario text already rules that out ('the root instructions file is already near its useful size limit'), so the key's alternative is a pre-excluded option rather than the nearest live one. Three of the four sheets independently named a nested CLAUDE.md at src/api/, which shares the path-scoped rule's defining property (lazy, subtree-conditional loading) and is the closer neighbour; it loses on narrower grounds (directory rather than glob scoping, and no re-injection after compaction). Graded to the key anyway: nested-CLAUDE.md answers scored 0.5, not 1.

Key says 'none', but the key's own failure_mode field is built on the 200-line / 25KB MEMORY.md index limit, and that limit is version-gated: per the sheets, v2.1.210 added the over-limit error, v2.1.211 stopped counting frontmatter and HTML comments toward it, v2.1.214 added the modified timestamp. This is the same shape as the pilot's S008 vs S003 finding: one field of the key concedes a version-dependent fact while version_caveat asserts there is none. Graded to the key: sheets citing those floors were not penalised and sheets asserting 'none' were not given extra credit.

Key says 'model', but the key's own rejection_reason says output styles 'modify the system prompt itself' and omit Claude Code's built-in software-engineering instructions unless keep-coding-instructions: true. Omitting that block is a deterministic client-side act, not a model choice, and it is precisely the property that makes the output style beat CLAUDE.md in this scenario. Three of four sheets answered 'harness owns the system-prompt construction, model owns holding the voice'. A flat 'model' key mis-states the layer that does the removal. Graded to the key by crediting splits that still assign voice and structure adherence to the model.

The key names 'author a custom plugin containing an .lsp.json entry that launches typescript-language-server'. That is the same mechanism as the primary (an LSP server delivered as a plugin component), differing only in provenance (official marketplace vs hand-rolled), not a different mechanism class. All four sheets independently named a PostToolUse hook running tsc --noEmit, which is the nearest genuinely distinct alternative for 'see compiler diagnostics after each edit'. Graded to the key, all four scored 0, so the field discriminates nothing in this scenario.

Key says 'none', but sibling keys in the same batch concede version gates on the same MCP authentication subsystem: S026 states v2.1.193 for the headersHelper re-run and retry, and S028 states v2.1.196 for the OAuth scope default. Three of four sheets independently name concrete gates (claude mcp login requires v2.1.186+, OAuth applies to the HTTP transport only). This is the same class of cross-key contradiction the pilot found between S008 and S003.

Key says 'n/a', but plugin-delivered skills, agents, and MCP tool definitions do occupy the main session context on every turn, which the /plugin detail view itself reports as a Context cost. Three of four sheets said exactly that. 'n/a' makes the field effectively ungradeable and hides a real, measurable context effect of the recommended mechanism.

The key's first clause ('no structured schema constrains usage, so the model can misuse flags a typed tool would have prevented') describes a design tradeoff of choosing bin/ over MCP, not a failure of the bin/ mechanism. No sheet named it. All four named the mechanism's actual failure surface (plugin disabled or not enabled in scope, missing executable bit or shebang, wrong OS/architecture binary, PATH injection scoped to the Bash tool only), which the key's second clause covers only in part.

Key names 'package the server configuration as a plugin and stand up an internal marketplace'. Three of four sheets instead named a user-scoped MCP server (claude mcp add --scope user, ~/.claude.json), which is arguably the nearer alternative because the scenario's binding constraints are 'arrives with a fresh clone' and 'no other repository will ever use this connection', and user scope is the mechanism that fails exactly those two constraints. The key's choice is defensible but is not obviously the nearest, and it cost three sheets the field.

The key says "none", but the same key's failure_mode states "project-level frontmatter hooks require workspace trust on v2.1.218+ or they are skipped". That is a version-gated fact about the recommended mechanism conceded inside one key while the version_caveat field denies any exists. Two sheets named exactly that gate and were graded down against "none". Same shape as the pilot's S008/S003 finding, except here the contradiction is inside a single key.

The key answers "model" and pairs it with a primary of restating the rule in each delegation prompt, yet the scenario's stated requirement is that the delegated searches stop touching vendor/, and the key's own failure_mode concedes the advisory answer cannot deliver that ("a hard guarantee needs a different mechanism entirely, such as a permissions deny rule, a PreToolUse hook, or denying Agent(Explore)"). All four sheets chose one of those three harness mechanisms, so every sheet scores 0 on primary, enforcement_owner and lifecycle for converging on the remedy the key itself names as the one that works. Graded to the key as instructed; the key rewards diagnosis of the docs' prescription over satisfaction of the user's requirement.

"none" is under-specified as a key and is not applied consistently across the batch. S040's key uses the scoped form ("none for the CLAUDE.md skip itself; v2.1.198+ ..."), so the bare "none" elsewhere is ambiguous between "the mechanism has no availability gate" and "no version fact is relevant". Here three sheets cite concrete gates on the recommended mechanism's behaviour (v2.1.198 background-by-default subagents, v2.1.211 completion notification, v2.1.212 spawn cap) that do not contradict subagents being ungated. I graded these 0.5 throughout rather than 0. Same issue recurs on S032 (v2.1.208 unresolvable tools list), S033 (v2.1.212 bare /btw, v2.1.187 arrow stepping), S036 and S038 (v2.1.215 preload exclusion).

The key names a remediation ("run in the main conversation and rely on /compact afterward") rather than a competing mechanism, which makes the field hard to grade against. Three of the four sheets independently named an inline skill holding the same run-and-summarize instructions, with the key's exact rejection reasoning (inline execution puts the log in the very context being protected). I scored those 0.5 because the named artifact differs from the key's, but the substance is the same contrast the key draws. If the intent was "anything that executes inline in the main conversation", the key should say so.

Key says "none" for /btw, yet three of four sheets independently and consistently report that bare /btw with no question requires v2.1.212 and that stepping between earlier answers requires v2.1.187. Independent convergence on the same two numbers suggests the caveat is real and the key is simply scoped to the core command without saying so. Recorded, not compensated for.

Systematic question mismatch. Every key in this batch answers failure_mode as 'what goes wrong if you use the REJECTED alternative' (e.g. S041 'With only a CLAUDE.md rule...', S047 'The hook version simply never runs', S050 'Plain -p produces environment-dependent results'). All 40 sheets answer it as 'how does the CHOSEN mechanism fail, open or closed'. Neither reading is unreasonable for a field named failure_mode, but as frozen the key and the answering prompt are asking different questions, so a literal grade-to-key would score all 40 sheets 0 and the field would carry zero signal about any arm. I graded the sheets on whether their failure analysis was substantively correct and consistent with the key's underlying open/closed distinction, applied identically to all four sheets, and flag it here rather than silently. Fix by either renaming the field (failure_if_wrong vs failure_mode) or rewriting the ten keys.

Key says 'harness'. All four sheets independently answered 'the model', each noting that the harness supplies only plumbing (mailbox files, file-locked shared task list, spawn) while whether the adversarial debate happens and whether the consensus is real are model behaviours nothing enforces. That is the same reading the keys themselves use in S042 and S049, where a skill and an output style are assigned 'model' because the harness delivers the text but the model owns the outcome. Under that consistent reading S048 should be 'model' or 'split', not 'harness'. Graded to the key anyway: 0.5 on all four sheets.

Key says 'external'. The rejection_reason in the same key credits MCP with 'a managed OAuth flow, and per-tool permissioning', both of which are Claude Code client functions, not the tracker's. All four sheets answered 'harness' or 'split, harness owns connection/OAuth/token storage/permission prompts', which matches the key's own prose better than the key's one-word label does. Contrast S047, where 'external' is unambiguously right because GitHub Actions runs the job entirely outside the harness. Graded to the key anyway: 0.5 on all four sheets.

Key says 'n/a'. A plugin has no single context boundary because its boundary is per component (skill description resident and body on demand in the main context, hooks out of process, MCP tool schemas resident once connected), which is exactly what all four sheets said. 'n/a' is not gradeable as written: a sheet that correctly explains the per-component answer looks like it contradicts a key that says the field does not apply. Suggest 'per component' as the key value.

Key says 'none', but three of the four sheets cite real, checkable version-scoped facts about this exact mechanism (hooks run without a controlling terminal as of v2.1.139; allowManagedHooksOnly and managed-policy settings as the non-overridable tier; exit 2 blocks while exit 1 does not). 'none' is defensible if it means 'no version gate on PreToolUse itself', but as a bare token it penalises the more accurate answers unless the grader reads it charitably, which is the same shape as the S008/S003 defect the pilot grader reported.

The key is the literal string "n/a", but every one of the 36 sheets in those nine scenarios answered the field substantively and plausibly (hook runs out of process, only the reason string or the denial crosses back, contents never enter the window). With no key content to grade against I could not mark any of them wrong, so all 36 scored 1.0. The field therefore adds a flat +1 to every arm in nine scenarios and discriminates nothing. Only S055, whose key says "main context", is a live field. Either give the other nine a real expected value or drop the field from the denominator.

The key names "a PostToolUse hook on Edit that reminds Claude to run tests" as the nearest alternative. All four sheets independently named the CLAUDE.md / verification-skill guidance route instead, which is the more natural near miss given the scenario explicitly stipulates the model forgetting. Graded to the key, so all four scored 0, meaning this field separates no arm in S055 and costs every arm equally.

The key names a Stop hook. For a request phrased as "we want an OS desktop alert", the nearest alternative is arguably the built-in notification channel (preferredNotifChannel / terminal bell), which two sheets named independently and rejected with correct reasoning about it not producing a true OS-level alert. One sheet named a PreToolUse toast. Only one of four hit the key. Graded to the key regardless, so three sheets scored 0 on what may be defensible answers.

The key names a PreToolUse Bash logging hook as the rejected alternative, but two of the four sheets used PreToolUse as a component of their primary design (Pre for the attempt, Post for the outcome) rather than as a discarded option, and all four named OpenTelemetry export or transcript parsing as the thing they actually rejected. The key's alternative behaves like a sub-part of the primary rather than a competing mechanism, which makes "nearest alternative" ambiguous here.

A load-bearing constraint sits only in rejection_reason, which is not a graded field: "no deny rule for aws may remain in settings since deny rules override hook allow decisions". Sheet 2 stated it explicitly and sheet 3 recommended the exact opposite ("keep a deny rule as a second layer", which would silently break the one approved command). Because the constraint is not attached to any graded field, correctly stating it earns nothing and contradicting it is only reachable as a wrong-detail deduction on failure_mode. Consider promoting it into the primary or failure_mode key.
